task_snapshots.title: Deduplicate Telegram bot subscribe/keyboard logic in telegram_bot.py
task_snapshots.description:
`app/core/telegram_bot.py` has significant duplication:

1. `subscribe_to_endpoint_callback` (lines ~325-409) and `subscribe_to_endpoint` (lines ~411-483) implement almost the same subscribe-or-activate logic against two different Update surfaces (callback query vs message). The only real difference is which reply method is called and how the endpoint is fetched.
2. `subscribe_command` (~150-196) and `refresh_endpoints_callback` (~525-566) both build an identical inline keyboard from the endpoint list and post the identical message text.
3. `handler_command` for `/unsubscribe` is currently wired to `list_subscriptions_command` — probably a copy/paste bug but confirm before changing behavior; if intentional, add a short comment noting so.

## What to change (ONLY this file)
1. Extract `_upsert_subscription(cur, endpoint_id: int, chat_id: str) -> tuple[str, str]` returning `(status, endpoint_name)` where status is one of `"already"`, `"reactivated"`, `"created"`. Both `subscribe_to_endpoint_callback` and `subscribe_to_endpoint` should call it and pick the right reply text from a small dict.
2. Extract `_build_endpoint_keyboard(endpoints: list[dict]) -> InlineKeyboardMarkup` and `_ENDPOINT_LIST_TEXT: str` module constants; use them in both `subscribe_command` and `refresh_endpoints_callback`.
3. For the `/unsubscribe` handler wiring: if it is a bug (users expect unsubscribe, not list), rewire to a new small handler that shows only unsubscribe buttons. If preserving old behavior, add a `# NOTE: /unsubscribe intentionally reuses /list to show the unsubscribe buttons inline.` comment on that line.
4. Preserve every user-facing message string exactly. No emoji or wording drift.
5. Do not touch the DB schema, other modules, or add tests (Task 1 owns tests).

## Files you own
`app/core/telegram_bot.py` — nothing else.

## Acceptance
- `grep -c "_upsert_subscription" app/core/telegram_bot.py` returns >= 3 (definition + 2 call sites).
- `grep -c "_build_endpoint_keyboard" app/core/telegram_bot.py` returns >= 3.
- `python -c "import app.core.telegram_bot"` exits 0.
- Net line count of the file drops by at least 80 lines vs before (there is ~180 lines of duplicate code).

task_snapshots.title: Extract startup notification logic out of app/__init__.py into app/core/startup.py
task_snapshots.description:
`app/__init__.py` is 228 lines because it inlines two big functions: `send_startup_notification` (async orchestrator) and `send_startup_notifications` (sync fan-out with duplicated Telegram loop). This violates the app-factory pattern and duplicates work already in `app/core/notifications.py`.

## What to change
1. Create NEW file `app/core/startup.py` and MOVE both functions there verbatim (preserve every string, log line, comment, and control flow). Fix imports so the moved code still resolves (`from .. import config`, `from ..db import get_db_connection`, `from .notifications import send_group_telegram_notification, send_ntfy_notification`).
2. In `app/__init__.py`:
   - Remove the two function bodies.
   - Add `from .core.startup import send_startup_notification` near the other core imports.
   - Leave `run_background_tasks` calling `send_startup_notification()` unchanged.
   - Remove the now-unused imports (`import requests` inside the deleted body was local; safe to drop). Keep everything else — do NOT touch `create_app`, the Flask setup, CORS, or the `/` route.
3. Do NOT deduplicate the inner Telegram loop against `send_telegram_notification` in this task — a follow-up task will do that once repositories exist. This task is a pure move + import fix so it stays reviewable.

## Files you own
`app/__init__.py` and NEW file `app/core/startup.py` — nothing else.

## Acceptance
- `app/core/startup.py` exists and defines `send_startup_notification` and `send_startup_notifications`.
- `grep -n "def send_startup_notification" app/__init__.py` returns nothing.
- `grep -n "def send_startup_notifications" app/__init__.py` returns nothing.
- `wc -l app/__init__.py` shows <= 110 lines (down from 228).
- `python -c "from app import create_app, run_background_tasks; from app.core.startup import send_startup_notification"` exits 0.
